newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco lawyers agree to release 7 Liggett papers.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco lawyers agree to release 7 Liggett papers.

text.p: Tobacco company lawyers on Monday agreed to the release of seven Liggett Group documents, which allegedly contain information on the hazards of nicotine.

These documents are among the papers that Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, pledged to turn over to anti-tobacco lawyers in a settlement in March with 22 state attorneys general suing cigarette makers.
Copies of the documents were not immediately available.
Bob Montgomery, an attorney representing the state of Florida in its lawsuit against tobacco companies, said before a hearing by a court-appointed special master that he had not seen the documents.

But he said he was told the documents support a state allegation "that there was a widespread conspiracy among all manufacturers to withhold information which they knew regarding the link between cigarettes and cancer and emphysema."

Speical Master William Rutter was asked to review the Liggett documents by the trial judge, Harold Cohen of Palm Beach County, to determine whether tobacco companies other than Liggett were entitled to keep them secret.
Lawyers for Florida argued the documents should be made public under the state's Sunshine Act because they contain information regarding public health hazards.

Thirteen other Liggett documents sought by Florida were still being reviewed by Rutter. The hearing is to resume on Tuesday, and Rutter is working against an April 14 deadline. His decisions are subject to review by Cohen.

During the hearing before Rutter, Bob Weber, an attorney for R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Co ,said there had been an oral agreement among the tobacco companies since 1954 to fight anti-tobacco suits jointly.

W.C. Gentry, an attorney for Florida, said that Weber's statement supported the state's claim that cigarette companies had conspired to hide the dangers of smoking in "a classic, racketeering" fashion.
